user.title: Add Modbus gateway
user.description: Enter the Modbus TCP gateway details. The integration will scan the RTU bus and create one Home Assistant device for each compatible meter.

data.limit_scan_range: Limit discovery to an address range

advanced.title: Advanced gateway settings
advanced.description: Auto detect tests both standard Modbus TCP and RTU-over-TCP by reading a real meter. A transparent gateway's RS485 baud and parity must already match the meters; those settings cannot be changed through generic Modbus TCP.

data.request_retries: Polling retries after the first attempt

scan_range.title: Modbus address range
scan_range.description: The default scan covers slave addresses 1 through 247. Restricting the range can make setup much faster.

tcd_layout.title: How are the TCDs wired?
tcd_layout.description: Found {found} meter(s). For each TCD, choose whether it measures one 3-phase load or three separate single-phase lines. Choose Not connected for a TCD that is not fitted; its sensors are then switched off and not polled.

tcd_names.title: Name the {tcd} line(s) on {meter}
tcd_names.description: {tcd} on {meter} measures a {mode}. Each line gets W, A, V and kWh sensors (a 3-phase load gets A and V per phase and one W and kWh total). Enter a long name, or pick an existing device to link its sensors to (its name is then used). The short name (R1, W1, ...) is used in entity IDs, and also as the label when a line has no long name. Leave a single-phase line completely empty if it is not connected. Leave everything empty, or tick Skip the rest, to set a TCD up later; Reconfigure pre-fills what you entered.

tcd_board.title: Distribution board for {meter}
tcd_board.description: Which distribution board is {meter} on (for example DB1)? Pick an existing device or type a name. The meter's device takes this name and it starts every sensor's entity ID, e.g. sensor.db1_r1_w. Leave both empty to keep the default name.

data.board_device: Or take the name from a device

progress.discover_devices: Scanning pass {pass}/{passes}, address {address}, using {transport}. Compatible meters found: {found}.

abort.unique_id_mismatch: The gateway address does not match this config entry.
abort.reconfigure_successful: Gateway settings and discovered meters were updated.

error.invalid_range: The first slave address must be less than or equal to the last slave address.
error.cannot_connect: Could not communicate with the gateway. Check its address, port, framing mode, and timeout, then try again.
error.no_devices_found: The gateway responded, but no compatible EM270, EM280, or EM24 meters were found. Check the RS485 settings, wiring, and slave-address range.

init.title: Polling options
init.description: {entities} sensors are enabled, which takes {reads} Modbus reads per poll (about {seconds} s on the bus). Recommended update interval for the highest resolution that keeps up: {recommended} s. Going lower makes polls overlap and slows everything down; enabling more sensors raises this. Use Reconfigure on the integration entry to change the gateway address, framing mode, scan range, wiring or names, or to rescan for meters.
